{{Short description|American-German nanoscientist}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=February 2024}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=February 2024}}
'''Cynthia Ann Volkert''' (born 1960) is a [[nanoscience|nanoscientist]] whose research focuses on the properties of [[nanoporous materials]], particularly metals including gold, other nano-scale metals, and their machining and fabrication using [[focused ion beam]]s, [[vapor deposition]], and [[dealloying]]. Born in the US, and educated in Canada and the US, she works in Germany as professor and director of the Institute for Materials Physics of the [[University of Göttingen]]. She is a former president of the {{ill|German Materials Society|de|Deutsche Gesellschaft für Materialkunde}} and of the [[Materials Research Society]].

==Education and career==
Volkert was born in 1960, in [[Williamsport, Pennsylvania]].{{r|dnb}} She studied physics at [[McGill University]] in Canada, graduating in 1982, and then went to [[Harvard University]] in the US for graduate study in physics. She earned a master's degree there in 1984, and completed her Ph.D. in 1987.{{r|cv|ug}} Her dissertation, ''Flow and Relaxation of Amorphous Metals'', was supervised by Frans Spaepen.{{r|harv}}

From 1988 until 1998 she worked in the US for [[Bell Labs]]. In 1999 she moved to the Max Planck Institute for Metals Research in [[Stuttgart]] (later part of the [[Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems]]), where she worked until 2002. Next, she became a researcher at Karlsruhe Research Center (now part of the [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]]), from 2003 to 2007. She took her current position as professor at the Institute for Materials Physics of the [[University of Göttingen]] in 2007.{{r|cv|ug}}

In 2008, Volkert became president of the {{ill|German Materials Society|de|Deutsche Gesellschaft für Materialkunde}}.{{r|cv}} In the same year she also became president of the [[Materials Research Society]].{{r|mrs}}

==Recognition==
Volkert was elected to the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]] in 2011.{{r|leo}}
